  id = {EDN-102},
  title = {FR-15's retrain trains on 60\,\% of the \texorpdfstring{\texttt{ES}}{ES} sellers and holds out the rest},
  date = {2026-11-05},
  milestone = {M6: Monitoring},
  topic = {Data Management, Model Evaluation, Monitoring},
  participants = {Lukas Häußler (decided), AI agents (options, implementation)},
  decision = {\texttt{split.\allowbreak{}holdout\_\allowbreak{}seller\_\allowbreak{}share: 0.\allowbreak{}4}: an \texttt{ES} seller whose hash of seed, \texttt{ES}, and seller key falls below 0.4 keeps its \texttt{ES} listings in the holdout, which the replay sends; the other \texttt{ES} sellers join the pool and the split rule is unchanged.
Their \texttt{ES} listings also enter FR-09's comparables index.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item All \texttt{ES} into training, replaying the old holdout: the replayed rows are in-sample, so any recovery is flattered.
\item A random row split of \texttt{ES}: the same dealer lands on both sides (EDN-14).
\item All \texttt{ES} in the pool, replaying \texttt{ES} in the test set: about 1,070 accepted requests, an empty holdout breaks \texttt{features}.
\item A share of 0.3: too few held-out requests for two drift windows of 1,000.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} The hash split moves no non-\texttt{ES} seller when the \texttt{ES} sellers join, so the models before and after differ only by the \texttt{ES} training rows.
A dry run kept 2,402 listings of 804 sellers out (2,266 accepted requests), put \texttt{ES} at 3.7\,\% of train, and passed the gate.},
  ai = {Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI laid out the options with measured row counts and recommended 0.4; it built the rule and dry-ran the retrain.
The dry run showed SC-05 at 91.8\,\%, 0.2 points under the band's top, against 91.0\,\% before.
An independent review reproduced the split and the dry run byte for byte, except the model's run metadata.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code session of 2026-11-05.
Question (translated from German): ``FR-15 rehearsal: How does ES get into the retraining? We need ES in training, but also ES sellers the new model has never seen, otherwise the `recovery' is flattered. Option A: a fixed share of the ES sellers stays held out (for the replay), the rest goes normally into train/val/test.''
Orchestrator briefing (core, paraphrased): ``Plan the FR-15 rehearsal with options for getting ES into training.''
Lukas answered: ``A, share 0.4 (recommended): 40\,\% of the ES sellers held out: about 2,460 replay rows, ES = 3.5\,\% of training.'' (translated from German)},
